tagline: From Ashton’s farmland through Teton Valley to a forested mountain road
intro: Farmland surrounds Ashton at the northern end of this drive. To the south, Teton Valley lies on the western slope of the Teton Range, with an economy rooted in agriculture and ranching and shifting toward recreational tourism. Paved highways run through the valley; beyond Victor, Idaho 31 crosses a mountainous part of Targhee National Forest south of Stouts Mountain.

Rail travel linked these towns before the present rail trail did. Union Pacific’s Teton Valley Branch was built from Ashton beginning in 1910 and reached Victor in 1912. The Ashton to Tetonia Trail opened in 2010 on part of that former line. It carries walkers, cyclists and horseback riders over a corridor once used by trains. The railroad also shifted local commerce: businesses moved from Haden to nearby Tetonia after it arrived. The modern trail crosses Conant Creek on a former railroad bridge, preserving a physical connection to that transport history.

Travel south from Ashton through Drummond and Felt on Idaho 32 toward Tetonia. Idaho 33 continues through Driggs to Victor, where Idaho 31 turns toward Swan Valley. That final stretch leaves the valley for the national forest, crosses North Pine Creek and Pine Creek, and reaches US 26 at Swan Valley.

moments.title: Ashton
moments.text: Ashton was founded in 1906, the same year its first scheduled trains arrived. Ashton became a winter rail terminus because the Yellowstone Branch north of town was left unplowed until spring. Dog teams provided winter transport into the snowbound country beyond. The first American Dog Derby, held in 1917, followed the unplowed branch for 55 miles from West Yellowstone to Ashton. A blizzard delayed the finish for two days. The next race used a figure-eight course through the open fields, bringing teams through town twice on each lap. Union Pacific brought spectators on special trains.

moments.title: Driggs
moments.text: Driggs stands in Teton Valley at the headwaters of the Teton River. Benjamin Woodbury Driggs, Jr. and Don Carlos Driggs founded the town in 1888. Union Pacific’s Teton Valley Branch linked Driggs with Ashton and Victor in 1912. Driggs is now the county seat, with Idaho 33 connecting it to Tetonia to the north and Victor to the south.

moments.title: Victor
moments.text: Victor formed in 1889 from four settlements: Trail Creek, Fox Creek, Chapin and Cedron. It took the name of mail carrier George Victor Sherwood. The railroad reached town in 1912. Its two-story depot served passengers and freight, with a freight room, baggage room and ticket office downstairs and crew layover quarters above. In 1928, an addition to the south provided a large waiting room, dressing rooms and restrooms. The building measures 150 feet by 26 feet. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1995.
